code_design_validator_result.summary: Independently re-verified every load-bearing factual claim in the design against real source (not the design's own citations): web/src/api/metrics.ts's parsePrometheusText and metricsApi.prometheusText() -> client.getText('/metrics') (unversioned) genuinely exist and MetricsPage.tsx genuinely consumes them; mix.lock line 19 confirms telemetry v1.4.2 already present transitively via bandit/db_connection/ecto/ecto_sql/plug/oidcc/thousand_island, with zero first-party :telemetry.execute call sites today; deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql.ex:900/1315 and deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo/supervisor.ex:30/55 confirm Ecto already emits [:letflow, :repo, :query] with no config/*.exs telemetry_prefix override; deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex:324-327 (match_path/1) and :520-528 (append_match_path/2) confirm the route-template composition claim exactly as cited; grepped web/src for /metrics and /api/v1/metrics -- no reference beyond router.tsx's admin/metrics UI route, MetricsPage.tsx, and metrics.ts itself, so removing lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex is safe; confirmed application.ex/poller.ex/event_store.ex citations (line numbers, existing patterns) are accurate. Adversarially audited the Axis 2/3 label-allowlist invariant against all six families individually, including a check for tenant-identifying route templates: lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex's forward table and every routers/*.ex file use only fixed, compile-time literal path segments with :id/:slug path PARAMETERS -- no per-tenant literal route segment exists anywhere in the router tree (R-Co's {tenant_id} path segment was already deliberately dropped per INV-1, per api_pipeline.ex's own moduledoc) -- so route_template cannot smuggle a tenant identifier even indirectly. No gap found. No implementation code fences present anywhere in the design doc -- all fenced blocks are @spec/@type only.

context.dependency_promotion_flag_for_reviewer: mix.exs change is `{:telemetry, "~> 1.4"}` ONLY. Confirmed precisely: :telemetry v1.4.2 is already resolved in mix.lock (line 19) as a TRANSITIVE dependency of bandit, db_connection, ecto, ecto_sql, plug, oidcc and thousand_island -- already fetched, compiled and running in every Letflow BEAM node today. Adding the explicit mix.exs line adds ZERO new bytes, zero new packages, zero new transitive tree, zero new NIF/Port/license surface -- it is a PROMOTION of an already-vendored transitive dependency to a direct one (standard Elixir hygiene: pin what you call directly), not a new-dependency adoption. This is materially lighter than REQ-148's {:lua, "~> 1.0"} precedent (which did fetch new bytes/a new transitive tree). REVIEWER sign-off is still required per REQ-194 AC3's own wording (draws no size-based exception), and the design (design doc section 10) does not unilaterally claim otherwise -- but REVIEWER should weigh it as a promotion-to-direct-dependency, not a new-dependency risk review, and record that distinction explicitly in sign-off.

task.description: Implement REQ-194 (Prometheus metrics subsystem, OBS-02) per the validated design at lib/letflow/design/req194-prometheus-metrics.md. Design has PASSED CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's gate (see code_design_validator_result above) -- implement exactly what it specifies: Letflow.Metrics.Registry (ETS-backed GenServer, lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex), Letflow.Metrics.Exposition (lib/letflow/metrics/exposition.ex), Letflow.Plugs.HttpMetrics (lib/letflow/plugs/http_metrics.ex), Letflow.Routers.MetricsExposition (lib/letflow/routers/metrics_exposition.ex) mounted at GET /metrics on Letflow.Router outside ApiPipeline/AuthPipeline, new :telemetry call sites in Letflow.Engine.complete_task/3 and Letflow.EventStore.append/2, the Letflow.Scheduler.Poller tick extension for the active-instances gauge with DB-unavailable graceful degradation, addition of {:telemetry, "~> 1.4"} to mix.exs deps/0 (see dependency_promotion_flag_for_reviewer -- flag for REVIEWER explicitly in the PR description regardless of its lighter risk profile), removal of lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex and its forward/test per design section 9, and the moduledoc restating design section 1's axis decisions verbatim per this requirement's own convention. Design sections 12 lists genuinely open implementation-time decisions (definition_status resolution path in complete_task/3; active-instances refresh cadence) -- use judgment there, design does not mandate a specific answer. Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test and quote real output; do not claim success without running them.
acceptance_criteria: this requirement states an explicit decision on each of REQ-078's three recorded divergences -- auth, scope and format -- with a reason for each, in the module moduledoc; it does not silently pick one or leave any of the three unstated

the format decision cites web/src/api/metrics.ts's parsePrometheusText and metricsApi.prometheusText()'s call to client.getText('/metrics') as an already-committed consumer contract, and the endpoint Letflow serves is one that web/src/pages/admin/MetricsPage.tsx actually reaches -- asserted by a test hitting that exact path

if a metrics dependency is added to mix.exs, REVIEWER sign-off is recorded for it in this requirement's PR; if instead a registry is hand-rolled, the moduledoc states that as the decision -- one or the other, not silence

all six OBS-02 core metric families are present in the exposition output after exercising the corresponding behaviour, asserted by parsing the response body -- not by asserting the emission call was made

the HTTP-request metric labels by route template and not by raw path: two requests to the same route with different path parameters produce ONE label combination, not two, asserted by counting distinct label sets in the output

the auth and scope decisions are enforced and tested: whichever position was taken, a test asserts that one tenant's scrape cannot observe another tenant's figures or identifiers (including through label values), or -- if the endpoint is deliberately global and unauthenticated -- that no metric label carries any tenant-identifying value at all
the exposition endpoint returns a successful response with the last known values when the database is unavailable, rather than erroring, asserted with the database made unreachable

instrumentation is emitted via :telemetry events and the registry attaches to them, so the emitting call sites do not reference the registry module directly, confirmed by grep over the instrumented modules
the disposition of lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex is explicit -- removed, or retained with its role stated in its own moduledoc -- and no route the SPA calls returns 404 afterwards
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
